args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the deploy of v2.3.1 (error rate 18%, unhealthy in us-east, us-west, eu-west). Per runbook, rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rollback status: rolled_out in us-east, us-west, eu-west. Next steps: confirm health checks and error rate recover on v2.3.0, and investigate root cause of the v2.3.1 regression (note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging) before any redeploy.

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what I did:

**Diagnosis**
- checkout-api was running v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy with an 18% error rate.
- Release history showed v2.3.0 as the most recent release that was healthy in production. (v2.3.1-rc was a staging-only, unhealthy build, so it was not a valid target.)

**Rollback**
- Rolled checkout-api back to **v2.3.0** in all production regions. Status: `rolled_out` in us-east, us-west, and eu-west.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001** (SEV2) for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. The summary documents the v2.3.1 failure, the rollback to v2.3.0, and suggested next steps (verify recovery on v2.3.0, root-cause the v2.3.1 regression before any redeploy — noting that v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging).

One recommendation: have someone confirm that health checks and the error rate actually recover on v2.3.0 over the next few minutes, since the rollback reports as rolled out but I haven't yet observed post-rollback health metrics.
